nodes.question: What are Product Service Systems (PSS) in the context of collaborative consumption?
nodes.answer: Product Service Systems (PSS) are a form of collaborative consumption under the sharing economy concept, involving tangible products and intangible services designed to meet specific customer needs.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Circular economy practices|Product sharing platforms_qna_003
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: How does immediate decision-making based on information sharing benefit the retailer in the product development process?
nodes.answer: Immediate decisions based on information sharing, especially regarding product performance and sustainability-related information, help the retailer to acquire the right product at the right time and price, enhancing efficiency in the development process.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Circular economy practices|Product sharing platforms_qna_004
nodes.label: Taxonomy
nodes.question: What do user-generated reviews on app-provision platforms like Google Play Store and Apple App Store help to understand?
nodes.answer: They help understand users' perceptions and feedback on the apps they use.
nodes.paragraph: As digital technology advances, numerous online platforms such as Twitter (officially known now as X), Instagram, Facebook and other specialised online forums have emerged, which serve as a virtual space for individuals to exchange their opinions, perspec- tives, and concerns, and they are becoming increas- ingly popular and influential in providing a real-time record of public sentiment (Arlt et al., 2018; Fronzetti Colladon, 2018). Research on such social media con- tent can offer a deeper understanding of the social perception, social contexts of specific policies, and potential solutions to bridge existing gaps (Li et al., 2019). Fronzetti Colladon, (2018) highlights that spontaneous consumer expressions can provide valua- ble insights into product features and user experience when analysed without creating a sense of surveil- lance. In this context, user-generated reviews on app- provision platforms such as Google Play Store and Apple App Store offer a useful means of understand- ing users perceptions and feedback on the apps they use (Cambria et al., 2016). These reviews serve as a valuable source of information, and systematically analysing the vast amount of user-generated content can help reveal evolving attitudes towards smart solu- tions, particularly in relation to household energy use (Genc-Nayebi & Abran, 2017; Mariani & Borghi, 2022).

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Circular economy practices|Product sharing platforms_qna_005
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: How many sectors and products are included in the SAM?
nodes.answer: The SAM contains 25 sectors and 26 products.
nodes.paragraph: ( 2022 ). The SAM is based on the 2019 data and represents the mutual interrela - tionships between the production structure, income distribution, and consumption patterns in Nigeria. The accounts included in the SAM are grouped into three main blocks: (a) fac - tors of production, (b) activities and products, (c) economic institutions. In the SAM, two types of production factors are represented: labor and capital. Additionally, the crop produc - tion sector utilizes a third production factor (land), which is considered as a specific type of capital for the sector. The SAM contains 25 sectors and 26 products, including fertilizers, which are entirely imported. Moreover, the agri-food sector is subdivided into four catego - ries: crop production, livestock, fisheries, and processed foods. The economic institutions in the SAM includes an external agent (the rest of the world) and three domestic agents (firms, government, and households). Furthermore, households are categorized regionally, includ - ing 6 geopolitical regions of Nigeria: South-South, South-East, South-West, North-Central, North-East, and North-West.
